unit: Ch 8: Provisions for Filing Return of Income and Self Assessment
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Return of Income: Meaning and Compulsory Filing
explain: A return of income is a formal statement of income, taxes paid, and tax payable for a tax year.
Companies, partnership firms, and universities or colleges must file a return whether they make a profit or loss.
Resident individuals holding foreign assets, foreign signing authority, or beneficial interest abroad must file mandatorily.
Other persons must file if their income before Chapter VIII and capital gain exemptions (sections 82 to 86) exceeds the basic exemption limit.
Filing is also compulsory if foreign travel spending exceeds ₹2 lakh, electricity bill exceeds ₹1 lakh, or current account deposits exceed ₹1 crore.
It is also mandatory if business turnover exceeds ₹60 lakh, professional receipts exceed ₹10 lakh, savings deposit reaches ₹50 lakh, or TDS/TCS is ₹25,000 or more (₹50,000 for senior citizens).

flow.title: Compulsory Filing Applicability Test
steps: Check if company or firm
If yes, filing is mandatory
If individual, check foreign asset holding
Check income before deductions against limit
Check high-value transaction criteria thresholds
File return if any condition is met

topics.example: Mr. A earns ₹3,80,000 but spends ₹2.5 lakh on a foreign vacation. He must file a return even though his total income is below ₹4,00,000.
remember: Basic exemption limit under default tax regime section 202(1) is ₹4,00,000.
Basic exemption under optional regime is ₹2,50,000 (₹3,00,000 for senior citizens, ₹5,00,000 for super senior citizens).
mistakes: Thinking a company does not need to file if it incurs a net loss.
Comparing income after Chapter VIII deductions with basic exemption limits instead of gross total income before deductions.

quiz.q: What is the basic exemption limit for an individual under the default tax regime u/s 202(1)?
quiz.why: The basic exemption limit under the default tax regime under section 202(1) is ₹4,00,000.

quiz.q: Under Rule 163, mandatory filing is triggered if aggregate electricity expenditure during the tax year exceeds:
quiz.why: Expenditure exceeding ₹1 lakh on electricity consumption mandates filing of return.

topics.title: Due Dates for Furnishing Return of Income
explain: The due date is the legal deadline in the financial year following the tax year to submit the return.
30th November applies to assessees required to submit a transfer pricing report under section 172, including their partners.
31st October applies to corporate assessees and non-corporate assessees subject to tax audit, including partners of audited firms.
31st August applies to non-audited assessees having business or professional profits, and partners of non-audited firms.
31st July applies to all other assessees, such as salaried employees and individuals with non-business income.

flow.title: Determining the Due Date
steps: Check if section 172 applies
If yes, due date is 30th November
If no, check corporate or audited status
If company or audited, 31st October
If non-audited business income, 31st August
All other assessees, 31st July

topics.example: A salaried individual with interest income and no business turnover has a filing due date of 31st July of the subsequent financial year.
remember: 30th November: Transfer pricing report u/s 172.
31st October: Companies and audited accounts.
31st August: Non-audited business/profession assessees.
31st July: Other assessees.
mistakes: Assuming all partners of a firm always have the same due date as salaried individuals.
Confusing the 31st August deadline for non-audited business assessees with the 31st July deadline for salaried individuals.

quiz.q: What is the due date for filing return for a domestic company not having international transactions?
quiz.why: Companies not requiring a section 172 report have a due date of 31st October.

quiz.q: The due date for a firm whose accounts are not required to be audited is:
quiz.why: Assessees with business income not requiring audit have a filing due date of 31st August.

topics.title: Belated Return and Revised Return
explain: A belated return can be filed if an assessee misses the original due date.
The time limit for a belated return is within 9 months from the end of the tax year (31st December) or before assessment completion, whichever is earlier.
A revised return can be furnished if an omission or wrong statement is discovered in an original or belated return.
The time limit for a revised return is within 12 months from the end of the tax year (31st March) or before assessment completion, whichever is earlier.
Once a return is revised, it completely substitutes the original return, and subsequent revisions are allowed within the permitted time.

flow.title: Filing Belated vs Revised Return
steps: Missed due date under 263(1)
File belated return before 31st December
Identify mistake in original or belated return
Check whether assessment is already completed
If not completed, file revised return
Ensure revised filing before 31st March

topics.example: For tax year 2026-27, a belated return can be filed up to 31st December 2027, and a revised return can be filed up to 31st March 2028 if assessment is not completed.
remember: Belated return deadline: 9 months from end of tax year (31st December).
Revised return deadline: 12 months from end of tax year (31st March).
Both deadlines terminate earlier if assessment is completed.
mistakes: Believing that a belated return cannot be revised.
Attempting to file a revised return after the Assessing Officer has completed assessment.

quiz.q: For tax year 2026-27, what is the outer time limit to submit a belated return if assessment is pending?
quiz.why: Belated return must be filed within 9 months from the end of the tax year, which is 31st December 2027.

quiz.q: Can an assessee file a revised return after assessment is completed if the 12-month period has not expired?
o: No, completion of assessment ends the opportunity
Yes, on payment of higher fees
quiz.why: A revised return can be filed before the completion of assessment or 12 months from tax year end, whichever is earlier.

topics.title: Updated Return of Income
explain: Any person can file an updated return within 48 months from the end of the financial year succeeding the relevant tax year.
It can be filed whether or not an original, belated, or revised return was filed previously.
An updated return cannot be a return of loss, decrease tax liability, or claim/increase an income tax refund.
If an original return claimed a loss, an updated return is allowed only if it turns it into positive income or reduces the loss.
Additional income tax payable is 25% (up to 12 months), 50% (12-24 months), 60% (24-36 months), or 70% (36-48 months) of aggregate tax and interest.
An updated return cannot be updated again once filed for that tax year.

flow.title: Updated Return Eligibility and Additional Tax
steps: Check if 48-month window is open
Ensure return does not reduce tax
Ensure no refund is created or increased
Verify updated return was not previously filed
Compute tax, interest, and late fee
Add applicable additional tax rate (25%-70%)
Pay total dues and submit return

topics.example: For tax year 2026-27, an updated return can be filed up to 31.03.2032 by paying tax, interest, and the slab-based additional tax.
remember: Time window: 48 months from the end of financial year succeeding the relevant tax year.
Additional tax rates: 25% (within 12m), 50% (12-24m), 60% (24-36m), 70% (36-48m).
mistakes: Filing an updated return to claim an additional tax refund or carry forward a higher loss.
Attempting to file a second updated return for the same tax year.

quiz.q: What is the additional tax percentage if an updated return is filed after 12 months but before 24 months from the relevant year end?
quiz.why: Between 12 and 24 months, the additional tax rate is 50% of aggregate tax and interest payable.

quiz.q: An updated return under section 263(6) can be filed to:
o: Declare additional income and pay additional tax
quiz.why: Updated returns cannot reduce tax liability, increase losses, or claim refunds; they are meant to report additional income.

topics.title: Defective Return
explain: A return is treated as defective if it is incomplete or fails to meet statutory requirements like missing schedules or audit reports.
The Assessing Officer informs the assessee and provides an opportunity to rectify the defect within 15 days.
The Assessing Officer may extend the 15-day period on an application submitted by the assessee.
If not rectified in time, the return is treated as an invalid return, as if no return was ever furnished.
If rectified after 15 days but before assessment is completed, the Assessing Officer may condone the delay and validate the return.

flow.title: Defective Return Rectification Process
steps: AO detects defect in return filed
AO issues intimation notice to assessee
Assessee receives 15 days to rectify
Assessee may request extension of time
If rectified within time, return is valid
If unrectified, return becomes invalid

topics.example: If an assessee subject to audit files a return without furnishing the audit report under section 63, the AO will issue a 15-day defect notice to rectify it.
remember: Default rectification period: 15 days from service of notice.
Unrectified defect leads to treating the return as invalid (void ab initio).
mistakes: Assuming that a defective return automatically leads to immediate tax penalties without giving 15 days to correct it.
Believing a return cannot be regularized once the 15 days pass, even if rectified before assessment.

quiz.q: Within how many days from the intimation must an assessee rectify a defective return?
quiz.why: Section 263(7) provides 15 days from intimation to rectify the defect, subject to further extension by the AO.

quiz.q: What is the legal consequence if a defect in the return is not rectified within the allowed time?
o: It is treated as a revised return
It is treated as an updated return
It is treated as an invalid return
It is assessed with a flat 200% penalty
quiz.why: Failure to rectify within the period causes the return to be treated as an invalid return as if never furnished.

topics.title: Interest and Fee for Default in Furnishing Return
explain: Interest under section 423 is charged at 1% simple interest per month or part of a month for late filing or non-filing.
The period runs from the due date under section 263(1) until the date of furnishing the return or completion of assessment.
Interest is calculated on the tax determined less advance tax, TDS/TCS, relief under section 157, and AMT credit.
Under section 428(a), a late filing fee of ₹1,000 applies if total income is up to ₹5,00,000, and ₹5,000 if it exceeds ₹5,00,000.
Under section 428(b), the same fee (₹1,000 or ₹5,00,000 threshold) applies if a revised return is filed beyond 9 months from the end of the tax year.

flow.title: Fee and Interest Computation
steps: Check if return furnished after due date
Calculate net unpaid assessed tax
Apply simple interest at 1% per month
Check total income level for fee
Add fee: ₹1,000 if income ≤ ₹5L
Add fee: ₹5,000 if income > ₹5L

topics.example: An individual with total income of ₹6,00,000 filing on 10th December pays a mandatory late fee of ₹5,000 plus 1% monthly interest on balance tax.
remember: Interest rate u/s 423: 1% simple interest per month or part thereof.
Fee u/s 428: ₹1,000 (income ≤ ₹5 lakh) or ₹5,000 (income > ₹5 lakh).
Fee u/s 428(b) applies to revised return filed after 9 months from tax year end.
mistakes: Levying a ₹5,000 late fee on taxpayers whose total income is below or equal to ₹5,00,000.
Calculating interest from the end of the financial year instead of from the due date of filing.

quiz.q: What is the fee payable under section 428(a) if an individual with total income of ₹4,80,000 files a belated return?
quiz.why: Where total income does not exceed ₹5,00,000, late fee under section 428 is restricted to ₹1,000.

quiz.q: What is the monthly interest rate charged under section 423 for default in furnishing return of income?
quiz.why: Section 423 levies simple interest at 1% per month or part of a month.

topics.title: Self-Assessment
explain: Before filing any return, the assessee must calculate and pay self-assessment tax, including interest and fees.
Tax payable is arrived at after subtracting advance tax, TDS/TCS, relief under section 157, and allowable AMT credit.
If the amount paid falls short of total dues, it is adjusted first towards fee, next towards interest, and the balance towards tax.
Default in paying full self-assessment dues makes the assessee an assessee-in-default.
Proof of payment of tax, interest, and fee must accompany the return of income.

flow.title: Order of Adjustment under Self-Assessment
steps: Assessee deposits short self-assessment amount
Amount first adjusted towards fee payable
Remaining amount adjusted towards interest
Residual amount adjusted towards tax
Unpaid balance treated as tax in default

topics.example: If ₹10,000 is paid against a liability of ₹2,000 fee, ₹3,000 interest, and ₹8,000 tax, ₹2,000 goes to fee, ₹3,000 to interest, and ₹5,000 to tax.
remember: Adjustment priority: 1. Fee -> 2. Interest -> 3. Tax payable.
Assessee becomes an assessee-in-default for any unpaid balance.
mistakes: Adjusting payments against tax principal first before clearing fee and interest.
Filing the return of income without paying self-assessment interest and fee.

quiz.q: In what order are short payments adjusted under section 266(3)?
quiz.why: Section 266(3) mandates adjustment first towards fee, then interest, and finally tax payable.

quiz.q: An assessee who fails to pay self-assessment tax before furnishing return is deemed to be:
quiz.why: Failure to pay full tax, interest, or fee renders the person an assessee in default.

topics.title: Tax Return Preparer Scheme
explain: The CBDT may frame a scheme enabling specified persons to prepare and file returns through Tax Return Preparers (TRPs).
A TRP is an authorized individual assisting taxpayers in preparing returns of income.
Specified class of persons covers any person other than a company or a person whose accounts are required to be audited u/s 63 or other law.
An officer of a scheduled bank with which the assessee maintains an account cannot act as a TRP.
Employees of the specified class of persons cannot act as a TRP, but employees of companies or audited persons can act as TRPs.

flow.title: TRP Eligibility Assessment
steps: Check taxpayer category
Exclude company and audited persons
Eligible taxpayer approaches authorized TRP
TRP assists and prepares return
Return submitted under notified scheme

topics.example: A small grocery proprietor whose turnover is ₹25 lakh (not subject to audit) can file through a TRP, whereas an audited trader cannot.
remember: Companies and audited entities cannot use a TRP.
Bank officers dealing with the assessee are prohibited from acting as their TRP.
mistakes: Thinking a private limited company can furnish its return using the TRP scheme.
Assuming individuals with audited accounts under section 63 can file through a TRP.

quiz.q: Who among the following CANNOT file their return through a Tax Return Preparer?
o: A retailer not liable to tax audit
quiz.why: Companies and persons whose accounts are subject to audit are excluded from the TRP scheme.

quiz.q: Can an employee of an audited corporate enterprise act as a TRP for an eligible individual?
o: Yes, because they are not employees of a specified class of person
Only if they are chartered accountants
quiz.why: Employees of companies/audited entities do not fall into the barred specified class and can act as TRPs.

topics.title: Persons Authorised to Verify Return of Income
explain: For an individual, the return must be verified by the individual himself, his guardian if mentally incapacitated, or a valid POA holder.
For a HUF, verification must be done by the Karta, or any other adult member if the Karta is absent from India or incapacitated.
For a company, verification must be done by the Managing Director, or any director if there is no MD or MD cannot verify for unavoidable reasons.
For a company undergoing corporate insolvency, verification must be done by the appointed insolvency professional.
For a firm, it is verified by the managing partner, or any adult partner if there is no managing partner or the managing partner is unable to act.
For an LLP, the designated partner verifies; if absent or unavailable, any partner or authority-appointed person can verify.

flow.title: HUF and Company Verification Rules
steps: HUF: Check if Karta is available
If absent from India, any adult member verifies
Company: Managing Director must verify
If no MD or unavailable, any director verifies
If under IBC, insolvency professional verifies
If wound up, court-appointed liquidator verifies

topics.example: If the Karta of a HUF is living in the UK, any adult member (male or female) of the HUF can validly sign and verify the return.
remember: Individual: Self / Guardian / POA holder.
HUF: Karta / Any adult member (if Karta absent or incapacitated).
Company: MD / Any director (if no MD or unavailable) / Liquidator / Insolvency Professional.
mistakes: Believing only male adult members can verify a HUF return when Karta is abroad.
Assuming an ordinary employee or non-director can verify a company's normal return.

quiz.q: When the Karta of a HUF is absent from India, who can verify the return of income?
o: Any adult member of the HUF
quiz.why: Section 265 allows any adult member (male or female) of the HUF to verify when the Karta is absent.

quiz.q: Who is authorised to verify the return of a company admitted to corporate insolvency resolution under the IBC?
o: Insolvency Professional appointed by Adjudicating Authority
quiz.why: Under section 265, the insolvency professional appointed by the adjudicating authority must verify the return.

topics.title: Permanent Account Number (PAN) and Aadhaar
explain: PAN application is mandatory if total income exceeds the basic exemption limit, or business turnover is likely to exceed ₹5 lakh.
Non-individual residents entering financial transactions of ₹2,50,000 or more and their key managerial persons must apply for PAN.
Cash deposits or withdrawals of ₹20 lakh or more in a year, or opening a current/credit account, require mandatory PAN application at least 7 days before.
Every person having PAN must link Aadhaar; failure to do so makes the PAN inoperative, blocking refunds and attracting higher TDS.
Under section 430, late intimation of Aadhaar attracts a fee up to ₹1,000; the inoperative PAN reactivates within 30 days of intimation and payment.
Section 467 imposes a penalty of ₹10,000 for each failure to apply, quote, or authenticate PAN/Aadhaar.

flow.title: Aadhaar Intimation and Inoperative PAN Flow
steps: Allotment of PAN to eligible person
Obligation to intimate Aadhaar number
Failure to intimate causes PAN to become inoperative
Consequences: No refunds, higher TDS u/s 397(2)
Pay late fee of ₹1,000 u/s 430
Intimate Aadhaar to tax authority
PAN becomes operative within 30 days

topics.example: A person whose PAN is inoperative due to unlinked Aadhaar cannot receive pending tax refunds until they pay ₹1,000 and complete linking.
remember: Cash deposit/withdrawal threshold for PAN: ₹20 lakh or more in a financial year.
Fee for delayed Aadhaar linking u/s 430: ₹1,000.
Penalty for non-compliance u/s 467: ₹10,000 per default.
mistakes: Thinking that an inoperative PAN is permanently canceled; it can be made operative within 30 days of paying ₹1,000 fee and intimating Aadhaar.
Assuming that possessing two PANs is allowed if one is personal and one is for proprietary business.

quiz.q: What is the penalty under section 467 for failing to quote or authenticate PAN in prescribed transactions?
quiz.why: Section 467 provides that the Assessing Officer may impose a penalty of ₹10,000 for each default.

quiz.q: Once an assessee pays the ₹1,000 fee and intimates Aadhaar, within how many days does the inoperative PAN become operative?
quiz.why: Under Rule 162, an inoperative PAN becomes operative within 30 days from the date of intimating Aadhaar.

topics.title: Mandatory Quoting of PAN in Prescribed Transactions
explain: Rule 159 mandates quoting PAN in key financial transactions to ensure transparency and track high-value dealings.
Mandatory for all credit card applications and opening demat/depository accounts.
Mandatory for purchasing motor vehicles (exceeding ₹5 lakh, excluding two-wheelers and tractors) and immovable property exceeding ₹20 lakh (or stamp value > ₹20 lakh).
Mandatory for payments exceeding ₹50,000 for acquiring RBI bonds, mutual funds, company debentures, or life insurance premium exceeding ₹50,000.
Mandatory for cash payment exceeding ₹1,00,000 for hotel/restaurant/banquet bills, and general goods/services purchases exceeding ₹2 lakh per transaction.
A person without PAN entering into specified transactions (Sl. 10 to 15) must make a declaration in Form No. 97.

flow.title: PAN Verification in Prescribed Transactions
steps: Assessee enters into specified financial transaction
Check transaction type against Rule 159 list
Check monetary threshold (e.g., > ₹50,000 or > ₹20L)
Quote PAN in relevant document
If no PAN, file declaration in Form No. 97
Recipient authenticates PAN/Aadhaar

topics.example: Buying a motor car for ₹8,00,000 requires mandatory quoting of PAN, but buying a farm tractor for ₹10,00,000 is specifically exempt.
remember: Immovable property threshold: Value exceeding ₹20 lakh.
Hotel cash bill threshold: Cash exceeding ₹1,00,000.
Motor vehicles: Exceeding ₹5 lakh (except tractors and two-wheelers).
Form for declaration when no PAN: Form No. 97.
mistakes: Quoting PAN for hotel bills paid by digital card when total bill is ₹1,00,000 (only cash exceeding ₹1,00,000 triggers the rule).
Applying the motor vehicle rule to tractors or two-wheelers.

quiz.q: Under Rule 159, quoting PAN is mandatory for purchasing immovable property if the transaction or stamp value exceeds:
quiz.why: Quoting PAN is required for purchase or sale of immovable property exceeding ₹20 lakh or valued by stamp authority over ₹20 lakh.

quiz.q: Which form must be filed as a declaration by a person who does not hold a PAN entering into transactions 10 to 15 of Rule 159?
quiz.why: The Income-tax Act, 2025 prescribes Form No. 97 for declaring transactions when the person does not have a PAN.
